facts.statement: The name Aniksosaurus means "spring lizard" because the holotype was discovered on September 21, 1995, which marked the beginning of spring in the Southern Hemisphere.
facts.quote: Aniksosaurus (meaning "spring lizard", from Modern Greek Άνοιξη, "Spring", referring to the fact it was found on 21 September 1995, the onset of Spring on the Southern Hemisphere)

facts.statement: Aniksosaurus darwini was formally described by Rubén Dario Martínez and Fernando Emilio Novas in 2006 from fossils found in the Bajo Barreal Formation.
facts.quote: The type species, Aniksosaurus darwini, was formally described from the Bajo Barreal Formation of the Golfo San Jorge Basin by Rubén Dario Martínez and Fernando Emilio Novas in 2006

facts.statement: The species name darwini honors Charles Darwin, who visited Patagonia in 1832 and 1833.
facts.quote: the specific epithet honors Charles Darwin who visited Patagonia in 1832/1833 during the Voyage of the Beagle

facts.statement: Aniksosaurus lived during the Cenomanian to Turonian stages of the Cretaceous period, approximately 96 to 91 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived during the Cenomanian to Turonian of the Cretaceous period, between 96-91 million years ago

facts.statement: Radiometric Ar-Ar dating confirms the Aniksosaurus fossils were deposited between the Cenomanian and Turonian stages, 96 to 91 million years ago.
facts.quote: The specimen was collected by Martínez in 1995 in green sandstone that was deposited between the Cenomanian stage and the Turonian stage of the Cretaceous period, between 96-91 million years ago, as shown by radiometric Ar-Ar dating

facts.statement: The type specimen of Aniksosaurus was discovered at the Laguna Palacios Ranch locality in the Bajo Barreal Formation of Chubut, Argentina.
facts.quote: The remains of the type specimen MDT-PV 1/48 were discovered in the Laguna Palacios Ranch locality in the lower Bajo Barreal Formation of Patagonia in Chubut, Argentina

facts.statement: The type specimen of Aniksosaurus consists of an articulated right hindlimb including the femur, fibula, tibia, and foot.
facts.quote: The type specimen MDT-PV 1/48, discovered in the Bajo Barreal Formation, consists of an articulated right hindlimb, which includes the femur, fibula, tibia and foot

facts.statement: The longest femur found for Aniksosaurus measures 247 mm, while the longest tibia measures 270 mm.
facts.quote: The longest femur discovered for this genus measures 247mm, and the longest tibia, 270mm

facts.statement: In Aniksosaurus, the tibia is on average 13% longer than the femur, an adaptation linked to cursorial (running) habits.
facts.quote: On average, the tibia is 13% longer than the femur in Aniksosaurus, an adaptation which has been strongly correlated with the development of cursorial habits in dinosaurs

facts.statement: Recent estimates suggest Aniksosaurus had a total body length between 2 and 3 meters and a weight between 35 and 45 kg.
facts.quote: However, recent estimates suggest a total body length between 2 m and 3 m and a body weight between 35 kg and 45 kg

facts.statement: A 2013 study concluded that the holotype and four other Aniksosaurus individuals were juveniles to sub-adults based on histological analysis.
facts.quote: In a 2013 study by Ibiricu et al., it was concluded that the holotype and four more individuals referable to Aniksosaurus, were juvenile to sub-adult individuals as shown by a histological analysis

facts.statement: Histological analysis of two Aniksosaurus individuals suggested they were approximately three years old.
facts.quote: The two individuals analyzed had histological characteristics that suggested an approximate age of three

facts.statement: Monospecific bonebeds suggest Aniksosaurus was gregarious, providing a selective advantage over competitors.
facts.quote: Monospecific bonebeds suggest it was gregarious, and that this behavior gave Aniksosaurus a selective advantage over competitors in its paleoenvironment

facts.statement: Aniksosaurus likely exhibited gregarious behavior only during a specific life stage, probably when it was a sub-adult.
facts.quote: Aniksosaurus is likely to have exhibited gregariousness only during a specific interval of its life, most likely when it was a sub-adult

facts.statement: Martínez and Novas (2006) originally classified Aniksosaurus within the clade Coelurosauria based on hindlimb anatomy.
facts.quote: Martínez and Novas (2006) originally assigned this genus to the clade Coelurosauria based on anatomical features present in the hindlimbs

facts.statement: Choiniere et al. (2010) found that Aniksosaurus is phylogenetically closer to members of the taxon Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Choiniere et al. (2010) demonstrated that phylogenetically, Aniksosaurus was closer to individuals in the taxon Compsognathidae

facts.statement: Hartman et al. (2019) classified Aniksosaurus as a maniraptoromorph outside the groups Compsognathidae and Maniraptora.
facts.quote: Hartman et al. (2019) instead find it to be a maniraptoromorph outside compsognathids and maniraptorans

facts.statement: Naish and Cau (2022) classified Aniksosaurus as a megaraptoran.
facts.quote: while Naish and Cau (2022) find it to be a megaraptoran

facts.statement: Aniksosaurus is classified within the unranked family Coelurosauria.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: Coelurosauria

facts.statement: The genus Aniksosaurus was established by Martínez & Novas in 2006.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Martínez & Novas, 2006

facts.statement: Aniksosaurus is distinguished by deep neural arches on cervical vertebrae, a wide neural canal, a ventral keel on caudal vertebrae, robust manual claws, narrow metatarsals and digit IV, an expanded brevis shelf on the ilium, and a deep notch on the femur.
facts.quote: According to Martínez and Novas (2006), Aniksosaurus can be distinguished based on the following characteristics: cranial cervical vertebrae have dorsoventrally deep neural arches, and are provided with a pair of cavities at their cranial surfaces the neural canal is wide cranial caudals feature a ventral sagittal keel, and their transverse processes are triangular-shaped in dorsal view manual ungual phalanges are robust the metatarsal and digit IV of the pes are transversely narrow ilium with an extremely expanded brevis shelf (a bone surface on the ilium that functions as an attachment site for tail muscles) the femur possesses a deep notch for the M. iliotrochantericus

facts.statement: Small scavengers likely fed on Aniksosaurus remains, evidenced by small grooves found on one of the recovered femora.
facts.quote: The soft tissue underwent subaerial weathering and then began to decompose, from the contributory action of small vertebrae scavengers as evidenced by a series of small grooves in one of the femora recovered

facts.statement: No evidence of cannibalism or intraspecific competition was found in the Aniksosaurus fossil assemblage.
facts.quote: No evidence was found to support either cannibalism or intra-specific competition

facts.statement: The Bajo Barreal Formation, where Aniksosaurus lived, also contained remains of Xenotarsosaurus, Drusilasaura, Epachthosaurus, Campylodoniscus, Secernosaurus, and teeth from carcharodontosaurids and dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: Dinosaur remains from this formation include those of the abelisaurid theropod Xenotarsosaurus bonapartei, the sauropods Drusilasaura, Epachthosaurus and Campylodoniscus, the hadrosaur Secernosaurus as well as indeterminate teeth belonging to carcharodontosaurids and dromaeosaurids

facts.statement: Remains of Aniksosaurus were found in 1995 in the current Chubut province, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos se encontraron en 1995 en la actual provincia de Chubut, Argentina y fueron publicados por la prensa argentina.

facts.statement: The type species Aniksosaurus darwini was officially described by Martínez and Novas in 2006, although the name was coined in 1997.
facts.quote: La especie tipo Aniksosaurus darwini, fue oficialmente descrita por Martínez y Novas en 2006, aunque el nombre fue acuñado en 1997.

facts.statement: The genus name refers to September 21, the day spring begins in the southern hemisphere and when the fossils were found.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se refiere al 21 de septiembre, día en que comienza la primavera en el hemisferio sur y en el que fueron encontrados los fósiles.

facts.statement: The species name honors Charles Darwin, who visited Patagonia between 1832 and 1833 on his voyage around the world on the Beagle.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie hace honores a Charles Darwin, quien visitara la Patagonia entre 1832 y 1833 en su viaje alrededor del mundo en el Beagle.

facts.statement: Remains were found in the lower part of the Bajo Barreal Formation in Patagonia, where at least five individuals were found in a bone bed with no other animals around.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron encontrados en la parte inferior de la Formación Bajo Barreal de la Patagonia, donde se hallaron por lo menos cinco individuos en una cama de huesos, sin ningún otro animal alrededor.

facts.statement: Five right tibias found at the discovery site indicate a minimum number of five individuals.
facts.quote: Cinco tibias derechas en el lugar del descubrimiento nos dan el número mínimo de individuos.

facts.statement: Remains were found in volcanic ash, indicating a volcano was dying out nearby.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron encontrados en cenizas volcánicas o que indica que había un volcán apagándose en las cercanías.

facts.statement: Martínez and Novas (2006) originally assigned this genus to the clade Coelurosauria based on anatomical characteristics present in the hind limbs.
facts.quote: Martínez y Novas (2006) originalmente asignadas a este género del clado Coelurosauria basado en características anatómicas presentes en los miembros posteriores.

facts.statement: However, more recent research by Choiniere et al. (2010) demonstrated that phylogenetically, Aniksosaurus was closer to Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo más recientes investigaciones de Choiniere et al. (2010) demostraron que filogenéticamente, Aniksosaurus estaba más cerca de Compsognathidae.

facts.statement: The parent group of Aniksosaurus is Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Compsognathidae

facts.statement: Aniksosaurus belongs to the family Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Family: Compsognathidae

facts.statement: The specimen was collected in 1995 from green sandstone deposited between the Cenomanian and Turonian stages of the Cretaceous, approximately 96 to 91 million years ago, as shown by Ar-Ar radiometric dating.
facts.quote: La muestra se recogió por Martínez en 1995 en piedra arenisca verde que fue depositada entre el Cenomaniano y el Turoniano del Cretácico, hace entre 96-91 millones de años, como se muestra por la datación radiométrica Ar-Ar.

facts.statement: Aniksosaurus lived from the Cenomanian to the Turonian, between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Monospecific bone beds suggest that Aniksosaurus was gregarious, and that this behavior gave it a selective advantage over competitors in its paleoenvironment.
facts.quote: Camas de huesos monoespecíficas sugieren que era gregario, y que este comportamiento dio Aniksosaurus una ventaja selectiva sobre los competidores en su paleoambiente.

facts.statement: It is probable that Aniksosaurus had a social life only during a specific interval of its life, most likely when it was a sub-adult.
facts.quote: Es probable que Aniksosaurus haya tenido vida social sólo durante un intervalo específico de su vida, lo más probable, cuando era un sub-adulto.

facts.statement: Soft tissue was exposed to subaerial weathering and began to decompose due to the concurrent action of small scavengers, as evidenced by a series of small grooves on one of the recovered femurs, followed by partial disarticulation of the skeleton.
facts.quote: El tejido blando se sometió a intemperie subaérea y luego comenzó a descomponerse, de la acción concurrente de los pequeños carroñeros como se evidencia por una serie de pequeñas ranuras en uno de los fémures recuperados, que luego fue seguido por la desarticulación parcial del esqueleto.

facts.statement: No evidence was found to support either cannibalism or intraspecific competition.
facts.quote: No se encontró evidencia para apoyar o bien el canibalismo o la competencia intraespecífica.

facts.statement: Remains of the type specimen MDT-PV 1/48 were discovered at the Laguna Rancho Palacios locality in the lower part of the Bajo Barreal Formation in Patagonia, Chubut, Argentina.
facts.quote: Los restos del espécimen tipo MDT-PV 1/48 fueron descubiertos en la localidad de Laguna Rancho Palacios, en la parte baja de la formación Bajo Barreal de la Patagonia en Chubut, Argentina.

facts.statement: Remains of at least four additional individuals, assigned as paratypes in 2006, were discovered at the site.
facts.quote: Los restos de al menos cuatro individuos más, en 2006 han sido asignado como paratipos, fueron descubiertos en el sitio.

facts.statement: Only one fossil occurrence of Aniksosaurus is recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

rejected.quote: Martinez and Novas (2006), based on femoral measurements, originally suggested that Aniksosaurus darwini was approximately 2 m long and 70 cm tall at the hip, and weighed up to 65 kg
